sentences.text: Shri Manuraj Singh, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri K. K. Tiwari, learned Govt. Advocate for the respo Heard on I.A.No.6833/2023, application for condonation of delay.
02. For the reasons stated in the application, I.A.No.6833/2023 stands allowed and disposed of.
Delay of 346 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
Heard on the question of admission.
Admit.

03. Also, heard o n I.A. No.6830/2023, which is first application filed under Section 389 of Cr.P.C.
for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant - Lakhan.

04. Learned Trial Court has convicted the appellant with 20 years R.I. with fine of Rs.3,000/- for the offence punishable u/s 376 of the IPC & 3/4 of POCSO Act, 5 years R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/-
for the offence punishable u/s 366(A) of the IPC and 3 years R.I. with fine for Rs.1,000/- for the offence punishable u/s 363 of the IPC with default stipulations, vide its judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 21.03.2022 passed by the learned First Additional Session Judge,
Sarangpur, District Rajgarh (Biora) (M.P.) in Special Trial No.322/2017.
05.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is further submitted that the complainant has made up a false story and given a contradictory statements.
The learned trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellant.
The FSL report (Ex.P/14) does not support the case of the prosecution.
The Dr. Sarita Yadav (PW-6) did not find any injury on the body of the victim.

This appeal is of year 2023 and final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, therefore, it is prayed that the substantial jail sentence of the appellant be suspended and he may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection by submitting that the trial Court after perusal of evidence available on record, convicted the appellant.

It is also submitted that the victim was a minor girl,
hence, the appellant is not entitled to grant benefit of suspension of sentence.
We have heard learned counsel for both the parties, perused the judgment and record of the trial Court.
07. As per the FIR, in the intervening night of 25-26 June, 2017, the victim left her home and the parents of the victim has lodged the FIR at Police Station Pachor, District - Rajgarh on 26.06.2017.
The victim was recovered on 09.07.2017.

Her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. was recorded as Exhibit-P/4 and in that she has stated that she was acquainted with the appellant and on 24-25 June, 2017 she herself went to the appellant's home and they performed the marriage at Shivalaya Mandir, Pachor.
She was beaten by her family members.

The prosecution witness Dr.
Sarita Yadav (PW-6) has not found any injury on the body of the victim.

08. Keeping in view the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties and that the final conclusion of this appeal will take considerable time,
we deem it fit to allow the application for suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of the appellant.

09. Accordingly, I.A. No.6830/2023 is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 24.09.2024 and on all other subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this behalf, the execution of substantial jail sentence imposed on the appellant Lakhan shall remain suspended, till final disposal of this appeal.
10. List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
